source: Rev 4/lugre_friction/Rev 4.2/model_parameters.json (Rev 4.2 parallel LuGre + nonlinear detent torque, 15-state)

notes.purpose: Partitions the Rev 4.2 model's parameters for a friction-parameter identification pass against the v3 hardware campaign. fixed_parameters are treated as known/given (geometry, inertia, structural stiffness/damping) and are not touched by the optimizer. current_dependent_parameters are derived per run from the actual drive/hold current rather than held at one constant value. variable_parameters are the LuGre friction parameters proposed for optimization, each with a starting value (copied from Rev 4.2's calibration) and a proposed bound -- review and adjust both before running anything.
notes.units: SI throughout: N, m, s, rad, N*m, N*m/rad, N*s/m, kg, kg*m^2, unless noted otherwise.
notes.review_needed: Bounds below are a first-pass proposal (roughly 0.1x-10x the current value, or a physically-motivated range for velocities/forces) -- not derived from any prior sensitivity study. Adjust before use.

N_r.description: Rotor tooth count / detent spatial frequency factor

T_d.description: Detent (cogging) torque amplitude -- from the motor's spec sheet (5 mN*m at 400 mA); distinct physical mechanism from LuGre friction; candidate to promote to variable_parameters later if the detent-torque panels don't fit well, but left fixed for now

c_nut.description: Nut structural damping -- DECIDED 2026-09-02: fixed to 0 to resolve double-counting with sigma1_nut/sigma2_nut (all three act on the same v_nut and are otherwise linearly indistinguishable at a single operating point). sigma1_nut/sigma2_nut now carry all nut-port dissipation; k_nut (the load-bearing spring) is unaffected.

smooth_velocity_epsilon.description: Numerical regularization for the LuGre smooth-abs(v) term, not a physical parameter

sigma1_target_zeta.description: Damping ratio used when the parent model derived sigma1 from sigma0 -- kept as a record; sigma1 itself is listed under variable_parameters below since the optimizer may want to move it independently

T_hold.description: Peak holding torque amplitude (drives k_em = N_r * T_hold, the motor's linearized electromagnetic stiffness). Rev 4.2's model_parameters.json hard-codes this at the 0.060 N*m / 400 mA nameplate value for every run; v3's six runs actually alternate between two current levels (200 mA and 400 mA peak, i.e. SC command value, hold current = run current per the v2 BACKLOG), so T_hold should be recomputed per run rather than held fixed. See README.md, "Current-dependent holding torque" for the state-space derivation and simulate_block_responses.py for the applied per-run override.

way.description: Linear guideway friction port (Jacobian couples to stage velocity x_n_dot directly)

sigma0_way.description: Bristle stiffness -- UPDATED 2026-09-03 from 7.6e5. Measured D_0.125 full-step treads at MRES 1/1 are visibly square (13% median creep fraction, not the ~59% 7.6e5 implies), bracketing presliding distance F_s,way/sigma0_way <= 1.3 um; 3.45e6 is that bound at the placeholder F_s_way=4.5 N. This is a LOWER bound, not a fitted point -- the true value could be higher (a timestamp-lag correction on the same measurement would tighten the bound further upward, not lower it). Bounds set to [3.45e6, 1.0e7] accordingly: do not let the optimizer search below the lower bound. See calibration_bracketing/RESULTS.md (step 4a) for the full derivation.

sigma1_way.description: Bristle damping (parent set via 2*zeta*sqrt(sigma0*M_s), zeta=0.7 -- coupled to sigma0_way if that relation is kept). NOT recomputed after sigma0_way's 2026-09-03 update -- at the new sigma0_way this value now implies zeta~0.33, not 0.7. Decide whether to recompute via the target-zeta rule or let the optimizer fit it independently of that rule before treating this as calibrated.

nut.description: Leadscrew-nut parasitic pre-rolling friction port (parallel to the k_nut/c_nut load path)

sigma1_nut.description: Bristle damping (parent set via 2*zeta*sqrt(sigma0*m_eff), m_eff = M_screw||M_s, zeta=0.7)

sb.description: Support bearing friction port (rotational, torque units -- Tc/Ts instead of Fc/Fs)
